It goes without saying that anyone who takes up, writes down, holds, preserves, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, what need to speak of whoever takes up this discourse on the Dharma, writes it, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and attends to it properly becoming endowed with the greatest wonder?

examples.dm: Subhūti, those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: "As many sentient beings as are included in the category of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warmth and moisture, or born miraculously; whether having form or without form; whether having perception or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—all those sentient beings I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa that leaves no remainder of the aggregates."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should form this thought: 'As many beings as are subsumed in the collection of beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from heat and moisture, or miraculously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, having no perception, or neither having nor lacking perception; however many are conceptually designated as the realm of beings—all these I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates.'
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेनैव चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-यावन्तः सुभूते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वधातौ सत्त्वसंग्रहेण संगृहीता अण्डजा वा जरायुजा वा संस्वेदजा वा औपपादुका वा रूपिणो वा अरूपिणो वा संज्ञिनो वा असंज्ञिनो वा नैवसंज्ञिनो नासंज्ञिनो वा, यावान् कश्चित्सत्त्वधातुः प्रज्ञप्यमानः प्रज्ञप्यते, ते च मया सर्वेऽनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: "Even though immeasurable sentient beings are thus led to complete nirvāṇa, one should generate the mind thinking that not even one sentient being has been led to complete nirvāṇa."

examples.dm: "Blessed One, it is wonderful how the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has so greatly benefited the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the supreme benefits, and how the Tathāgata has so greatly entrusted the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the supreme entrustments. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!"

examples.gm: Blessed One, the supreme benefit with which the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened Buddha has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and the supreme entrustment with which the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings—it is wonderful, O Blessed One! It is wonderful, O Sugata!
examples.sa: आश्चर्यं भगवन्,परमाश्चर्यं सुगत,यावदेव तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वा अनुपरिगृहीताः परमेणानुग्रहेण। आश्चर्यं भगवन् यावदेव तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वाः परीन्दिताः परमया परीन्दनया।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas arises from this.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, the unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening of the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas arises from this;
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? अतोनिर्जाता हि सुभूते तथागतानामर्हतां सम्यक्संबुद्धानामनुत्तरा सम्यक्संबोधिः,

examples.dm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement.
examples.gm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? अहमस्मि भगवंस्तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन अरणाविहारिणामग्र्यो निर्दिष्टः। अहमस्मि भगवन् अर्हन् वीतरागः।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in phenomena.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts without abiding in objects.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते न बोधिसत्त्वेन वस्तुप्रतिष्ठितेन दानं दातव्यम्,

examples.dm: Subhūti, in this way a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in the perception of characteristics.
examples.gm: Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts in such a way that they do not abide even in the notion of a sign.
examples.sa: एवं हि सूभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन महासत्त्वेन दानं दातव्यं यथा न निमित्तसंज्ञायामपि प्रतितिष्ठेत्।

examples.dm: Why is that? Because whatever abides is itself non-abiding.
examples.gm: Why is that? Because whatever is an abiding is itself a non-abiding.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? यत्प्रतिष्ठितं तदेवाप्रतिष्ठितम्।

examples.dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
examples.gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?
examples.sa: अस्ति स कश्चिद्धर्मो यस्तथागतेनानुत्तरा सम्यक्संबोधिरित्यभिसंबुद्धः,

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, there is neither truth nor falsehood in the phenomena that the Tathāgata has perfectly awakened to or taught.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, in whatever phenomena the Tathāgata has fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते यस्तथागतेन धर्मोऽभिसंबुद्धो देशितो निध्यातः, न तत्र सत्यं न मृषा।

examples.dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?
examples.gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?
examples.sa: अस्ति स कश्चिद्धर्मो यस्तथागतेन दीपंकरस्य तथागतस्यान्तिकादनुत्तरां सम्यक्संबोधिमभिसंबुद्धः ?

examples.dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
examples.gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?
examples.sa: अस्ति स कश्चिद्धर्मो यस्तथागतेनानुत्तरा सम्यक्संबोधिरित्यभिसंबुद्धः,

examples.dm: One should generate the mind for unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment.
examples.gm: give rise to the mind for unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment.
examples.sa: अनुत्तरायां सम्यक्संबोधौ चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्।

examples.dm: All those sentient beings will have my awakening placed upon their shoulders.
examples.gm: and all those sentient beings will carry my awakening upon their shoulders.
examples.sa: सर्वे ते सुभूते सत्त्वाः समांशेन बोधिं धारयिष्यन्ति वचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति।

examples.dm: If some son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm world system with the seven kinds of precious substances and give them as a gift, would that son or daughter of noble family generate much merit on that basis?
examples.gm: If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?
examples.sa: यः कश्चित्कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा इमं त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रं लोकधातुं सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, अपि नु स कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा ततोनिदानं बहु पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयात्।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up this Dharma discourse, hold it, keep it, read it, master it, and extensively and correctly teach it to others are known by the Tathāgata, and are seen by the Tathāgata;
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up, hold, keep, read, completely comprehend, and vastly and authentically teach to others this dharma discourse, they are known by the Tathāgata, seen by the Tathāgata, and
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते ये कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा इमं धर्मपर्यायमुद्ग्रहीष्यन्ति धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति, ज्ञातास्ते सुभूते तथागतेन बुद्धज्ञानेन, दृष्टास्ते सुभूते तथागतेन बुद्धचक्षुषा, बुद्धास्ते तथागतेन।

examples.dm: Subhūti, if I were to describe the mass of merit of those noble sons or noble daughters who would fully uphold as much of this mass of merit as there is, sentient beings would become bewildered and their minds would be troubled.
examples.gm: Subhūti, if I were to express the heap of merit of those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family, however great a heap of merit those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family will fully hold at that time, sentient beings would go mad and their minds would be confounded.
examples.sa: सचेत्पुनः सुभूते तेषां कुलपुत्राणां कुलदुहितॄणां वा अहं पुण्यस्कन्धं भाषेयम्, यावत्ते कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा तस्मिन् समये पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसविष्यन्ति, प्रतिग्रहीष्यन्ति, उन्मादं सत्त्वा अनुप्राप्नुयुश्चित्तविक्षेपं वा गच्छेयुः।

examples.dm: The Tathāgata’s Possession of the Five Extraordinary Eyes
examples.gm: The Tathāgata Possessing the Five Extraordinary Eyes

examples.dm: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the fleshly eye?
examples.gm: "Subhūti, what do you think? Does the Tathāgata possess the physical eye?"
examples.sa: भगवानाह-तत्किं मन्यसे सुभूते-संविद्यते तथागतस्य मांसचक्षुः ?

examples.dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the divine eye?
examples.gm: "Does the Tathāgata possess the divine eye?"
examples.sa: संविद्यते तथागतस्य दिव्यं चक्षुः ?

examples.dm: Blessed One, if I were to think that I had attained the state of an arhat, the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, "The son of good family, Subhūti, is the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement."
examples.gm: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained Arhatship,' the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions;
examples.sa: सचेन्मम भगवन्नेवं भवेत्-मया अर्हत्त्वं प्राप्तमिति, न मां तथागतो व्याकरिष्यदरणाविहारिणामग्र्यः सुभूतिः कुलपुत्रो

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up this Dharma discourse, hold it, keep it, read it, master it, and extensively and correctly teach it to others are known by the Tathāgata, and are seen by the Tathāgata;
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up, hold, keep, read, completely comprehend, and vastly and authentically teach to others this dharma discourse, they are known by the Tathāgata, seen by the Tathāgata, and
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते ये कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा इमं धर्मपर्यायमुद्ग्रहीष्यन्ति धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति, ज्ञातास्ते सुभूते तथागतेन बुद्धज्ञानेन, दृष्टास्ते सुभूते तथागतेन बुद्धचक्षुषा, बुद्धास्ते तथागतेन।

examples.dm: Subhūti, if I were to describe the mass of merit of those noble sons or noble daughters who would fully uphold as much of this mass of merit as there is, sentient beings would become bewildered and their minds would be troubled.
examples.gm: Subhūti, if I were to express the heap of merit of those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family, however great a heap of merit those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family will fully hold at that time, sentient beings would go mad and their minds would be confounded.
examples.sa: सचेत्पुनः सुभूते तेषां कुलपुत्राणां कुलदुहितॄणां वा अहं पुण्यस्कन्धं भाषेयम्, यावत्ते कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा तस्मिन् समये पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसविष्यन्ति, प्रतिग्रहीष्यन्ति, उन्मादं सत्त्वा अनुप्राप्नुयुश्चित्तविक्षेपं वा गच्छेयुः।

examples.dm: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra Entitled The Diamond-Cutter Perfection of Wisdom
examples.gm: The Noble Mahayana Sutra Called the Diamond Cutter Perfection of Wisdom

examples.dm: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond" is concluded.
examples.gm: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra called the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā is complete.
examples.sa: आर्यवज्रच्छेदिका भगवती प्रज्ञापारमिता समाप्ता॥

examples.dm: Subhūti, the name of this Dharma discourse is the Perfection of Wisdom;
examples.gm: Subhūti, the name of this discourse on the Dharma is the Perfection of Wisdom, and
examples.sa: प्रज्ञापारमिता नामायं सुभूते धर्मपर्यायः।

examples.dm: Blessed One, how should one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
examples.gm: O Blessed One, how should one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
examples.sa: तत्कथं भगवन् बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन कुलपुत्रेण वा कुलदुहित्रा वा स्थातव्यं

examples.dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the path of the bodhisattva should know, see, and resolve to understand all phenomena in this way:
examples.gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, thus should those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle know, see, and be resolved upon all dharmas,
examples.sa: भगवानाह-एवं हि सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन सर्वधर्मा ज्ञातव्या द्रष्टव्या अधिमोक्तव्याः।

examples.dm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
examples.gm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle dwell?
examples.sa: कथं भगवन् बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन स्थातव्यम्,

examples.dm: and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
examples.gm: grasp at a sentient being, grasp at a living soul, and grasp at a person.
examples.sa: सत्त्वग्राहो जीवग्राहः पुद्गलग्राहो भवेत्।

examples.dm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a Stream-Enterer were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer', that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.sa: सचेद्भगवन् स्रोतआपन्नस्यैवं भवेत्- मया स्रोतआपत्तिफलं प्राप्तमिति, स एव तस्यात्मग्राहो भवेत्,

examples.dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life force, and grasping at a person.
examples.gm: It would be grasping at a living being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.
examples.sa: सत्त्वग्राहो जीवग्राहः पुद्गलग्राहो भवेदिति॥

examples.dm: Subhūti, because of that, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should generate the mind in such a way that it does not abide.
examples.gm: Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva, a great being, should produce the mind without dwelling in this way;
examples.sa: तस्मात्तर्हि सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन महासत्त्वेन एवमप्रतिष्ठितं चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यं

examples.dm: How should the mind be held?
examples.gm: How should they fully control their minds?
examples.sa: कथं चित्तं प्रग्रहीतव्यम् ?

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, I fully know the streams of thought of all the sentient beings that exist in those world systems, with their various and diverse intentions.
examples.gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, I fully know the streams of mind of various dispositions of however many sentient beings there are in those world realms."
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यावन्तः सुभूते तेषु लोकधातुषु सत्त्वाः, तेषामहं नानाभावां चित्तधारां प्रजानामि।

examples.dm: Subhūti, the name of this Dharma discourse is the Perfection of Wisdom;
examples.gm: Subhūti, the name of this discourse on the Dharma is the Perfection of Wisdom, and
examples.sa: प्रज्ञापारमिता नामायं सुभूते धर्मपर्यायः।

examples.dm: For those supreme perfections that have been spoken of by the Tathāgata have also been spoken of by immeasurable and countless Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
examples.gm: because whatever supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata, that has also been taught by immeasurable, boundless Buddhas, Bhagavāns.
examples.sa: यां च सुभूते तथागतः परमपारमितां भाषते, तामपरिमाणा अपि बुद्धा भगवन्तो भाषन्ते।

examples.dm: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond" is concluded.
examples.gm: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra called the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā is complete.
examples.sa: आर्यवज्रच्छेदिका भगवती प्रज्ञापारमिता समाप्ता॥

examples.dm: The Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s park, together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks and a vast number of bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
examples.gm: The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jetavana, the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great saṅgha of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks, and very many bodhisattvas, great beings.
examples.sa: भगवान् श्रावस्त्यां विहरति स्म जेतवनेऽनाथपिण्डदस्यारामे महता भिक्षुसंघेन सार्थं त्रयोदशभिर्भिक्षुशतैः संबहुलैश्च बोधिसत्त्वैर्महासत्त्वैः।

examples.dm: Subhūti, because of that, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should generate the mind in such a way that it does not abide.
examples.gm: Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva, a great being, should produce the mind without dwelling in this way;
examples.sa: तस्मात्तर्हि सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन महासत्त्वेन एवमप्रतिष्ठितं चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यं

examples.dm: The Tathāgata has benefited the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the most sublime of benefits.
examples.gm: The Tathāgata has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme benefit.
examples.sa: अनुपरिगृहीतास्तथागतेन बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वाः परमेणानुग्रहेण।

examples.dm: "Blessed One, it is wonderful how the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has so greatly benefited the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the supreme benefits, and how the Tathāgata has so greatly entrusted the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the supreme entrustments. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!"
examples.gm: Blessed One, the supreme benefit with which the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened Buddha has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and the supreme entrustment with which the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings—it is wonderful, O Blessed One! It is wonderful, O Sugata!
examples.sa: आश्चर्यं भगवन्,परमाश्चर्यं सुगत,यावदेव तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वा अनुपरिगृहीताः परमेणानुग्रहेण। आश्चर्यं भगवन् यावदेव तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वाः परीन्दिताः परमया परीन्दनया।

examples.dm: "Sugata, that body would be large."
examples.gm: Sugata, that body would be large.
examples.sa: महान् सुगत स आत्मभावो भवेत्।

examples.dm: “They are many, Sugata.”
examples.gm: Sugata, they are many.
examples.sa: बहु सुगत पृथिवीरजो भवेत्।

examples.dm: Blessed One, in the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, will there be any sentient beings who will arise to form a correct perception of such explanations of the words of a sutra as this?
examples.gm: Blessed One, will there appear any sentient beings in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?
examples.sa: अस्ति भगवन्। केचित्सत्त्वा भविष्यन्त्यनागतेऽध्वनि पश्चिमे काले पश्चिमे समये पश्चिमायां पञ्चशत्यां सद्धर्मविप्रलोपकाले वर्तमाने, ये इमेष्वेवंरूपेषु सूत्रान्तपदेषु भाष्यमाणेषु भूतसंज्ञामुत्पादयिष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: Subhūti, those who will attain even a single moment of faith of mind regarding such explanations of the sūtra as this, the Tathāgata knows them.
examples.gm: Subhūti, the Tathāgata knows those who will obtain even a single thought of faith regarding the teaching of a sūtra such as this.

examples.dm: Subhūti, those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: "As many sentient beings as are included in the category of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warmth and moisture, or born miraculously; whether having form or without form; whether having perception or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—all those sentient beings I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa that leaves no remainder of the aggregates."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should form this thought: 'As many beings as are subsumed in the collection of beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from heat and moisture, or miraculously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, having no perception, or neither having nor lacking perception; however many are conceptually designated as the realm of beings—all these I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates.'
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेनैव चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-यावन्तः सुभूते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वधातौ सत्त्वसंग्रहेण संगृहीता अण्डजा वा जरायुजा वा संस्वेदजा वा औपपादुका वा रूपिणो वा अरूपिणो वा संज्ञिनो वा असंज्ञिनो वा नैवसंज्ञिनो नासंज्ञिनो वा, यावान् कश्चित्सत्त्वधातुः प्रज्ञप्यमानः प्रज्ञप्यते, ते च मया सर्वेऽनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven types of precious jewels and give them as a gift, and if a bodhisattva were to gain patience in the realization that phenomena are without self and unborn, then that bodhisattva would generate a mass of merit far greater, immeasurable, and incalculable than that.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven precious things and give them as a gift, and if a Bodhisattva were to attain the patience that this Dharma-discourse is selfless and unproduced, he would produce from that basis a mass of merit vastly greater, incalculable and immeasurable.

examples.sa: संविद्यते तथागतस्य प्रज्ञाचक्षुः ?

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if those bodhisattva mahāsattvas were to engage in the perception of phenomena, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because if those bodhisattva great beings engage in the perception of a dharma, they would by that very fact grasp at a self,
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? सचेत्सुभूते तेषां बोधिसत्त्वानां महासत्त्वानां धर्मसंज्ञा प्रवर्तेत, स एव तेषामात्मग्राहो भवेत्,

examples.dm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a Stream-Enterer were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer', that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.sa: सचेद्भगवन् स्रोतआपन्नस्यैवं भवेत्- मया स्रोतआपत्तिफलं प्राप्तमिति, स एव तस्यात्मग्राहो भवेत्,

examples.dm: Subhūti, if the Tathāgata were to liberate any sentient being whatsoever, that would be the Tathāgata grasping at a self.
examples.gm: Subhūti, if the Tathāgata were to have liberated any sentient beings whatsoever, that itself would be an apprehension of a self by the Tathāgata,
examples.sa: यदि पुनः सुभूते कश्चित्सत्त्वोऽभविष्यद्यस्तथागतेन परिमोचितः स्यात्, स एव तथागतस्यात्मग्राहोऽभविष्यत्,

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm of great thousand-fold world systems with the seven types of precious substances and give them as a gift, and if another were to take up from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and explain it to others and correctly demonstrate it, they would generate a mass of merit from that basis that is far greater, incalculable, and immeasurable.
examples.gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, compared to some son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, whoever takes up even just a four-line verse from this discourse on dharma, teaches it to others, and perfectly explains it will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता व इमं त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रं लोकधातुं सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भ्यः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य परेभ्यो विस्तरेण देशयेत् संप्रकाशयेत्, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयादप्रमेयसंख्येयम्।

examples.dm: and were to offer them as gifts to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, compared to that, if someone were to take up even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse, and were to correctly explain and correctly teach it to others, that person would generate much more merit on that basis—countless and measureless merit."
examples.gm: compared to giving them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly and fully awakened Buddhas, if someone were to take up even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma, explain it fully and correctly to others, and teach it fully and correctly, they would produce infinitely and immeasurably much more merit from that basis.
examples.sa: तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य परेभ्यो देशयेत् संप्रकाशयेत्, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयादप्रमेयमसंख्येयम्॥११॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any son or daughter of noble family were to gather a heap of the seven precious substances equal in size to as many Mount Merus, the kings of mountains, as there are in the trichiliocosm, and give them as a gift, and if another person were to take from this Perfection of Wisdom even just a four-line stanza and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit would not approach even a hundredth part of the latter, nor would it bear comparison, even up to the point of calculation.
examples.gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who, having collected heaps of the seven precious substances equal in amount to however many Sumerus, kings of mountains, there are in the three thousand grand thousand world systems, gives them as a gift, if someone were to take up even just a single four-line stanza from this perfection of wisdom and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this one, up to not even bearing comparison.
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभुते स्त्री वा पुरुषो वा यावन्तस्त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रे लोकधातौ सुमेरवः पर्वतराजानः, तावतो राशीन् सप्तानां रत्नानामभिसंहृत्य तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा इतः प्रज्ञापारमिताया धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य परेभ्यो देशयेत्, अस्य सुभूते पुण्यस्कन्धस्य असौ पौर्वकः पुण्यस्कन्धः शततमीमपि कलां नोपैति, यावदुपनिषदमपि न क्षमते॥२४॥

examples.dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall accomplish the adornment of the buddha-fields,' he would be speaking untruthfully."
examples.gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I will accomplish the array of the fields,' they would be speaking falsely.
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यः कश्चित्सुभूते बोधिसत्त्व एवं वदेत्-अहं क्षेत्रव्यूहान् निष्पादयिष्यामीति, स वितथं वदेत्।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva were to say, "I shall accomplish the arrays of buddhafields," that should also be spoken of in that same way.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall accomplish the arrays of the fields,' he too would be spoken of in the same way.
examples.sa: यः सुभूते बोधिसत्त्व एवं वदेत्- अहं क्षेत्रव्यूहान्निष्पादयिष्यामीति, स वितथं वदेत्।

examples.dm: Therefore, it is called "adornment of the buddha-fields."
examples.gm: therefore, they are called 'the array of the fields.'
examples.sa: तेनोच्यन्ते क्षेत्रव्यूहा इति।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall accomplish the adornment of the buddha-fields,' he would be speaking untruthfully."
examples.gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I will accomplish the array of the fields,' they would be speaking falsely.

examples.sa: तेनोच्यन्ते क्षेत्रव्यूहा इति।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a shrine for the world including gods, humans, and asuras. It goes without saying that anyone who takes up, writes down, holds, preserves, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, what need to speak of whoever takes up this discourse on the Dharma, writes it, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and attends to it properly becoming endowed with the greatest wonder?
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते यस्मिन् पृथिवीप्रदेशे इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य भाष्येत वा संप्रकाश्येत वा, स पृथिवीप्रदेशश्चैत्यभूतो भवेत् सदेवमानुषासुरस्य लोकस्य, कः पुनर्वादो ये इमं धर्मपर्यायं सकलसमाप्तं धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति। परमेण ते सुभूते आश्चर्येण समन्वागता भविष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and if there were as many world systems as there are grains of sand in all those rivers, would those world systems be numerous?
examples.gm: "If there were just as many river Gaṅgās as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, and if there were as many world realms as there are grains of sand in those, do you think those world realms would be many?"
examples.sa: यावत्यो गङ्गायां महानद्यां वालुकाः, तावत्य एव गङ्गानद्यो भवेयुः, तासु वा वालुकाः, तावन्तश्च लोकधातवो भवेयुः, कच्चिद्बहवस्ते लोकधातवो भवेयुः ?

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, I fully know the streams of thought of all the sentient beings that exist in those world systems, with their various and diverse intentions.
examples.gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, I fully know the streams of mind of various dispositions of however many sentient beings there are in those world realms."
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यावन्तः सुभूते तेषु लोकधातुषु सत्त्वाः, तेषामहं नानाभावां चित्तधारां प्रजानामि।

examples.dm: They should practice generosity without abiding in form.
examples.gm: Without abiding in form, they should give gifts.
examples.sa: न रूपप्रतिष्ठितेन दानं दातव्यम्।

examples.gm: He has not entered into forms, nor into sounds, nor into smells, nor into tastes, nor into tangible objects, nor into dharmas;

examples.gm: they should produce the mind without dwelling on form.

examples.dm: Likewise, they should practice generosity without abiding in sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, or phenomena.
examples.gm: Likewise, without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tactile objects, or mental phenomena, they should give gifts.

examples.dm: Blessed One, in the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, will there be any sentient beings who will arise to form a correct perception of such explanations of the words of a sutra as this?
examples.gm: Blessed One, will there appear any sentient beings in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?
examples.sa: अस्ति भगवन्। केचित्सत्त्वा भविष्यन्त्यनागतेऽध्वनि पश्चिमे काले पश्चिमे समये पश्चिमायां पञ्चशत्यां सद्धर्मविप्रलोपकाले वर्तमाने, ये इमेष्वेवंरूपेषु सूत्रान्तपदेषु भाष्यमाणेषु भूतसंज्ञामुत्पादयिष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, do not speak like that. Do not say, "In the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, will there be any sentient beings who will arise to form a correct perception of such explanations of the words of a sutra as this?"
examples.gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, do not speak like this, saying: "Will there appear any sentient beings in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?"
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः

examples.dm: Why is that? Blessed One, those sentient beings who will generate a correct perception regarding this explanation of the sutra will be endowed with supreme marvels.
examples.gm: Why is that? Bhagavān, those sentient beings who will generate a true perception regarding this sūtra being taught will be endowed with supreme wonder.
examples.sa: परमेण ते भगवन् आश्चर्येण समन्वागता बोधिसत्त्वा भविष्यन्ति, ये इह सूत्रे भाष्यमाणे श्रुत्वा भूतसंज्ञामुत्पादयिष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: If some son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm world system with the seven kinds of precious substances and give them as a gift, would that son or daughter of noble family generate much merit on that basis?
examples.gm: If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?
examples.sa: यः कश्चित्कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा इमं त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रं लोकधातुं सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, अपि नु स कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा ततोनिदानं बहु पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयात्।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up this Dharma discourse, hold it, keep it, read it, master it, and extensively and correctly teach it to others are known by the Tathāgata, and are seen by the Tathāgata;
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up, hold, keep, read, completely comprehend, and vastly and authentically teach to others this dharma discourse, they are known by the Tathāgata, seen by the Tathāgata, and
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते ये कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा इमं धर्मपर्यायमुद्ग्रहीष्यन्ति धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति, ज्ञातास्ते सुभूते तथागतेन बुद्धज्ञानेन, दृष्टास्ते सुभूते तथागतेन बुद्धचक्षुषा, बुद्धास्ते तथागतेन।

examples.dm: Subhūti, if I were to describe the mass of merit of those noble sons or noble daughters who would fully uphold as much of this mass of merit as there is, sentient beings would become bewildered and their minds would be troubled.
examples.gm: Subhūti, if I were to express the heap of merit of those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family, however great a heap of merit those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family will fully hold at that time, sentient beings would go mad and their minds would be confounded.
examples.sa: सचेत्पुनः सुभूते तेषां कुलपुत्राणां कुलदुहितॄणां वा अहं पुण्यस्कन्धं भाषेयम्, यावत्ते कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा तस्मिन् समये पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसविष्यन्ति, प्रतिग्रहीष्यन्ति, उन्मादं सत्त्वा अनुप्राप्नुयुश्चित्तविक्षेपं वा गच्छेयुः।

examples.dm: The Tathāgata has spoken this Dharma discourse for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the unsurpassed vehicle.
examples.gm: The Tathāgata has spoken this dharma discourse for the sake of sentient beings who have authentically entered into the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of sentient beings who have authentically entered into the foremost vehicle.
examples.sa: अयं च सुभूते धर्मपर्यायस्तथागतेन भाषितोऽग्रयानसंप्रस्थितानां सत्त्वानामर्थाय, श्रेष्ठयानसंप्रस्थितानां सत्त्वानामर्थाय।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the path of the bodhisattva should know, see, and resolve to understand all phenomena in this way:
examples.gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, thus should those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle know, see, and be resolved upon all dharmas,
examples.sa: भगवानाह-एवं हि सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन सर्वधर्मा ज्ञातव्या द्रष्टव्या अधिमोक्तव्याः।

examples.dm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
examples.gm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle dwell?
examples.sa: कथं भगवन् बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन स्थातव्यम्,

examples.dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has declared that all phenomena are the qualities of a Buddha.
examples.gm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has taught that all dharmas are the Buddha's dharmas.
examples.sa: तस्मात्तथागतो भाषते-सर्वधर्मा बुद्धधर्मा इति।

examples.dm: Subhūti, what are called "all phenomena" are all non-phenomena.
examples.gm: Subhūti, as for what is called 'all dharmas,' they are all non-dharmas.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? सर्वधर्मा इति सुभूते अधर्मास्तथागतेन भाषिताः।

examples.dm: Therefore, all phenomena are called the qualities of a Buddha.
examples.gm: Therefore, all dharmas are called the Buddha's dharmas.
examples.sa: तस्मादुच्यन्ते सर्वधर्मा बुद्धधर्मा इति॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a noble son or a noble daughter were to take all the earth-dust particles in the trichiliocosm world-system and reduce them to a collection of the finest atoms, what do you think, Subhūti? Would that collection of the finest atoms be numerous?
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any son of good family or daughter of good family were to grind as many particles of earth as there are in the trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world system, into powder so that they become, for example, like a mass of fine atoms, what do you think, Subhūti, would that mass of fine atoms be large?
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा यावन्ति त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रे लोकधातौ पृथिवीरजांसि, तावतां लोकधातूनामेवंरूपं मषिं कुर्यात् यावदेवमसंख्येयेन वीर्येण तद्यथापि नाम परमाणुसंचयः, तत्किं मन्यसे सुभूते-अपि नु बहुः स परमाणुसंचयो भवेत् ?

examples.dm: That collection of the finest atoms would be numerous."
examples.gm: that mass of fine atoms would be large.
examples.sa: बहुः स परमाणुसंचयो भवेत्।

examples.dm: Why is that? Bhagavan, if a collection of the finest atoms were to exist, the Bhagavan would not have spoken of a "collection of the finest atoms."
examples.gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a mass of fine atoms existed, the Blessed One would not have spoken of a "mass of fine atoms".
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? सचेद्भगवन् बहुः परमाणुसंचयोऽभविष्यत्, न भगवानवक्ष्यत्-परमाणुसंचय इति।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in phenomena.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts without abiding in objects.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते न बोधिसत्त्वेन वस्तुप्रतिष्ठितेन दानं दातव्यम्,

examples.dm: Why is that? Because the Tathāgata has taught that it is without any real entity.
examples.gm: Why is that? Because the Tathāgata has taught it as being no entity;
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? आत्मभाव आत्मभाव इति भगवन् न भावः स तथागतेन भाषितः।

examples.dm: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, just as a person with sight who enters the darkness sees nothing at all, so should one view a bodhisattva who practices generosity while having fallen into the perception of entities.
examples.gm: Subhūti, it is like this: just as a person with eyes who enters into darkness sees nothing at all, in the same way should a bodhisattva be seen who has fallen into objects when giving gifts.
examples.sa: तद्यथापि नाम सुभूते पुरुषोऽन्धकारप्रविष्टो न किंचिदपि पश्येत्, एवं वस्तुपतितो बोधिसत्त्वो द्रष्टव्यो यो वस्तुपतितो दानं परित्यजति।

examples.dm: Likewise, they should practice generosity without abiding in sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, or phenomena.
examples.gm: Likewise, without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tactile objects, or mental phenomena, they should give gifts.
examples.sa: न शब्दगन्धरसस्प्रष्टव्यधर्मेषु प्रतिष्ठितेन दानं दातव्यम्।

examples.sa: तेनोच्यन्ते बुद्धधर्मा इति॥८॥

examples.gm: Does a Stream-Enterer think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer'?
examples.sa: अपि नु स्रोतआपन्नस्यैवं भवति-मया स्रोतआपत्तिफलं प्राप्तमिति?

examples.gm: therefore he is called a Stream-Enterer.

examples.dm: Does a once-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a once-returner'?"
examples.gm: Does a Once-Returner think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner'?
examples.sa: अपि नु सकृदागामिन एवं भवति-मया सकृदागामिफलं प्राप्तमिति ?

examples.dm: Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of being a once-returner.
examples.gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that has entered into the state of a Once-Returner;
examples.sa: स सकृदागामिन एवं भवति-मया सकृदागामिफलं प्राप्तमिति। तत्कस्य हेतोः ? न हि स कश्चिद्धर्मो यः सकृदागामित्वमापन्नः।

examples.dm: Therefore, it is called a "once-returner."
examples.gm: therefore he is called a Once-Returner.
examples.sa: तेनोच्यते सकृदागामीति॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "adornment of the buddha-fields" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as a non-adornment, because those adornments do not exist.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'the array of the fields, the array of the fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught them as being no array;
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? क्षेत्रव्यूहाः क्षेत्रव्यूहा इति सुभूते अव्यूहास्ते तथागतेन भाषिताः।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva were to say, "I shall accomplish the arrays of buddhafields," that should also be spoken of in that same way.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall accomplish the arrays of the fields,' he too would be spoken of in the same way.
examples.sa: यः सुभूते बोधिसत्त्व एवं वदेत्- अहं क्षेत्रव्यूहान्निष्पादयिष्यामीति, स वितथं वदेत्।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "arrays of buddhafields, arrays of buddhafields"—the Tathāgata has said that they are not arrays.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of the fields, arrays of the fields', the Tathāgata has taught them as being without array.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? क्षेत्रव्यूहाः क्षेत्रव्यूहा इति सुभूते अव्यूहास्ते तथागतेन भाषिताः।

examples.dm: If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, would the grains of sand in all those rivers be numerous?"
examples.gm: If there were just as many Gaṅgā rivers as there are grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river, would you think that the grains of sand in them would be many?
examples.sa: यावत्यो गङ्गायां महानद्यां वालुकास्तावत्य एव गङ्गानद्यो भवेयुः ? तासु या वालुकाः, अपि नु ता बह्वयो भवेयुः ?

examples.dm: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, those Ganges Rivers themselves would be numerous, so what need is there to mention the grains of sand in them?"
examples.gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, if those Gaṅgā rivers themselves would be many, what need to speak of their grains of sand?
examples.sa: सुभूतिराह-ता एव तावद्भगवन् बह्वयो गङ्गानद्यो भवेयुः, प्रागेव यास्तासु गङ्गानदीषु वालुकाः।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if a man or a woman were to abandon as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges river, and if someone else were to take up even a four-line stanza from this discourse on Dharma and teach it to others, that person would generate far more merit, immeasurable and incalculable."
examples.gm: The Bhagavān said, "Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, and if someone were to retain from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and teach it properly to others, this one would generate on that basis far greater, incalculable, immeasurable merit."
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते स्त्री वा पुरुषो वा दिने दिने गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, एवं परित्यजन् गङ्गानदीवालुकासमान् कल्पांस्तानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, यश्च इतो धर्मपर्यायदन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्यपरेभ्यो देशयेत् संप्रकाशयेत्, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयादप्रमेयमसंख्येयम्॥१३॥

examples.dm: Do you think that the number of dust motes in the great trichiliocosm world system is many?”
examples.gm: Do you think that the particles of earth that exist in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system are many?"
examples.sa: यावत् त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रे लोकधातौ पृथिवीरजः कच्चित्, तद्बहु भवेत् ?

examples.dm: Subhūti, those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: "As many sentient beings as are included in the category of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warmth and moisture, or born miraculously; whether having form or without form; whether having perception or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—all those sentient beings I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa that leaves no remainder of the aggregates."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should form this thought: 'As many beings as are subsumed in the collection of beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from heat and moisture, or miraculously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, having no perception, or neither having nor lacking perception; however many are conceptually designated as the realm of beings—all these I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates.'
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेनैव चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-यावन्तः सुभूते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वधातौ सत्त्वसंग्रहेण संगृहीता अण्डजा वा जरायुजा वा संस्वेदजा वा औपपादुका वा रूपिणो वा अरूपिणो वा संज्ञिनो वा असंज्ञिनो वा नैवसंज्ञिनो नासंज्ञिनो वा, यावान् कश्चित्सत्त्वधातुः प्रज्ञप्यमानः प्रज्ञप्यते, ते च मया सर्वेऽनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: "I shall lead all sentient beings to final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I will lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन एवं चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-सर्वे सत्त्वा मया अनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall lead sentient beings to complete nirvana,' that one should not be called a bodhisattva.
examples.gm: If any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall cause sentient beings to completely pass into nirvāṇa,' he would not be called a bodhisattva.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व एवं वदेत्-अहं सत्त्वान् परिनिर्वापयिष्यामिति, न स बोधिसत्त्व इति वक्तव्यः।

examples.dm: "Even though immeasurable sentient beings are thus led to complete nirvāṇa, one should generate the mind thinking that not even one sentient being has been led to complete nirvāṇa."
examples.gm: One should generate the mind thinking: 'Even though immeasurable beings have thus been led to complete nirvāṇa, no being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.'
examples.sa: एवमपरिमाणानपि सत्त्वान् परिनिर्वाप्य न कश्चित्सत्त्वः परिनिर्वापितो भवति।

examples.dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in anything at all.

examples.sa: यन्न क्वचित्प्रतिष्ठितं चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्।

examples.dm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings are led to final nirvāṇa in this way, one should generate the mind with the thought that not even one sentient being has been led to final nirvāṇa.
examples.gm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings have been led to complete nirvāṇa in this way, no sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa'—thus should they generate the mind.
examples.sa: एवं स सत्त्वान् परिनिर्वाप्य न कश्चित्सत्त्वः परिनिर्वापितो भवति।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a shrine for the world including gods, humans, and asuras. examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते यस्मिन् पृथिवीप्रदेशे इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य भाष्येत वा संप्रकाश्येत वा, स पृथिवीप्रदेशश्चैत्यभूतो भवेत् सदेवमानुषासुरस्य लोकस्य, कः पुनर्वादो ये इमं धर्मपर्यायं सकलसमाप्तं धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति। परमेण ते सुभूते आश्चर्येण समन्वागता भविष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where this sūtra is taught will be worthy of being venerated by the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a shrine for the world including gods, humans, and asuras. It goes without saying that anyone who takes up, writes down, holds, preserves, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, what need to speak of whoever takes up this discourse on the Dharma, writes it, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and attends to it properly becoming endowed with the greatest wonder?

examples.dm: Should the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha be perceived by means of those thirty-two marks of a great being?"
examples.gm: Should the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the fully awakened Buddha be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?"
examples.sa: द्वात्रिंशन्महापुरुषलक्षणैस्तथागतोऽर्हन् सम्यक्संबुद्धो द्रष्टव्यः ?

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those thirty-two marks of a great being that the Tathāgata has spoken of were spoken of by the Tathāgata as being without marks.
examples.gm: Why is that? Because whatever thirty-two marks of a great man were taught by the Tathāgata, they were taught by the Tathāgata as not marks.
examples.sa: द्वात्रिंशन्महापुरुषलक्षणैस्तथागतोऽर्हन् सम्यक्संबुद्धो द्रष्टव्यः।तत्कस्य हेतोः ? यानि हि तानि भगवन् द्वात्रिंशन्महापुरुषलक्षणानि तथागतेन भाषितानि, अलक्षणानि तानि भगवंस्तथागतेन भाषितानि।

examples.dm: Therefore, they are called the thirty-two marks of a great being.
examples.gm: Therefore they are called the thirty-two marks of a great man."
examples.sa: तेनोच्यन्ते द्वात्रिंशन्महापुरुषलक्षणानीति॥

examples.gm: Should the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the fully awakened Buddha be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?"

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, this supreme perfection of wisdom has been spoken of by the Tathāgata.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, this supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata,
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? परमपारमितेयं सुभूते तथागतेन भाषिता यदुतापारमिता।

examples.dm: For those supreme perfections that have been spoken of by the Tathāgata have also been spoken of by immeasurable and countless Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
examples.gm: because whatever supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata, that has also been taught by immeasurable, boundless Buddhas, Bhagavāns.
examples.sa: यां च सुभूते तथागतः परमपारमितां भाषते, तामपरिमाणा अपि बुद्धा भगवन्तो भाषन्ते।

examples.dm: Therefore, it is called the supreme perfection.
examples.gm: Therefore, it is called the supreme perfection.
examples.sa: तेनोच्यन्ते परमपारमितेति॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any man or woman were to sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the morning, and likewise sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the midday, and again sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the evening, and in this way were to sacrifice their body for many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons;
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the morning, and were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā at midday and in the afternoon, compared to giving away bodies in this manner for many tens of millions, hundreds of millions, and hundreds of thousands of eons,
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते स्त्री वा पुरुषो वा पुर्वाह्णकालसमये गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, एवं मध्याह्नकालसमये गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, सायाह्नकालसमये गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, अनेन पर्यायेण बहूनि कल्पकोटिनियुतशतसहस्राण्यात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्,

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven types of precious jewels and give them as a gift, and if a bodhisattva were to gain patience in the realization that phenomena are without self and unborn, then that bodhisattva would generate a mass of merit far greater, immeasurable, and incalculable than that.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven precious things and give them as a gift, and if a Bodhisattva were to attain the patience that this Dharma-discourse is selfless and unproduced, he would produce from that basis a mass of merit vastly greater, incalculable and immeasurable.
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा गङ्गानदीवालुकासमाँल्लोकधातून् सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च बोधिसत्त्वो निरात्मकेष्वनुत्पत्तिकेषु धर्मेषु क्षान्तिं प्रतिलभते, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसवेदप्रमेयमसंख्येयम्।

examples.dm: If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and if there were as many world systems as there are grains of sand in all those rivers, would those world systems be numerous?
examples.gm: "If there were just as many river Gaṅgās as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, and if there were as many world realms as there are grains of sand in those, do you think those world realms would be many?"
examples.sa: यावत्यो गङ्गायां महानद्यां वालुकाः, तावत्य एव गङ्गानद्यो भवेयुः, तासु वा वालुकाः, तावन्तश्च लोकधातवो भवेयुः, कच्चिद्बहवस्ते लोकधातवो भवेयुः ?

examples.dm: The venerable Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, that which the Tathāgata has spoken of as a person possessing a human body and a great body, the Tathāgata has spoken of as having no body."
examples.gm: Venerable Subhūti said, "Blessed One, as for what the Tathāgata has taught as 'a person endowed with a human body and having a large body', the Tathāgata has taught that as being without a body.
examples.sa: आयुष्मान् सुभूतिराह- योऽसौ भगवंस्तथागतेन पुरुषो भाषित उपेतकायो महाकाय इति, अकायः स भगवंस्तथागतेन भाषितः।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, I fully know the streams of thought of all the sentient beings that exist in those world systems, with their various and diverse intentions.
examples.gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, I fully know the streams of mind of various dispositions of however many sentient beings there are in those world realms."
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यावन्तः सुभूते तेषु लोकधातुषु सत्त्वाः, तेषामहं नानाभावां चित्तधारां प्रजानामि।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "stream of thought" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as being without a stream.
examples.gm: "Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'stream of mind, stream of mind', the Tathāgata has taught it to be no stream."
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? चित्तधारा चित्तधारेति सुभूते अधारैषा तथागतेन भाषिता,

examples.dm: Therefore, it is called a "stream of thought."
examples.gm: "Therefore it is called 'stream of mind'."
examples.sa: तेनोच्यते चित्तधारेति।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, I fully know the streams of thought of all the sentient beings that exist in those world systems, with their various and diverse intentions.
examples.gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, I fully know the streams of mind of various dispositions of however many sentient beings there are in those world realms."
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यावन्तः सुभूते तेषु लोकधातुषु सत्त्वाः, तेषामहं नानाभावां चित्तधारां प्रजानामि।
