examples.dm: Therefore, it is called a "stream of thought."
examples.gm: "Therefore it is called 'stream of mind'."
examples.sa: तेनोच्यते चित्तधारेति।

examples.dm: Subhūti, the past mind is also unapprehendable.
examples.gm: Subhūti, the past mind cannot be apprehended.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? अतीतं सुभूते चित्तं नोपलभ्यते।

examples.dm: The future mind is also unapprehendable.
examples.gm: The future mind cannot be apprehended.
examples.sa: अनागतं चित्तं नोपलभ्यते।

examples.dm: It is because the present mind is also unapprehendable.
examples.gm: Because the present mind cannot be apprehended.
examples.sa: प्रत्युत्पन्नं चित्तं नोपलभ्यते॥१८॥

examples.dm: it is perfectly and completely awakened through all wholesome dharmas.
examples.gm: it is fully awakened to by means of all wholesome dharmas.
examples.sa: सर्वैः कुशलैर्धर्मैरभिसंबुध्यते।

examples.dm: Subhūti, as for what are called "wholesome dharmas," the Tathāgata has taught that they are devoid of the nature of dharmas;
examples.gm: Subhūti, as for what are called 'wholesome dharmas', the Tathāgata has spoken of them as being exactly non-dharmas;
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? कुशला धर्माः कुशला धर्मा इति सुभूते अधर्माश्चैव ते तथागतेन भाषिताः।

examples.dm: therefore, they are called "wholesome dharmas."
examples.gm: therefore they are called 'wholesome dharmas'.
examples.sa: तेनोच्यन्ते कुशला धर्मा इति॥२३॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not take hold of a mass of merit.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a Bodhisattva should not fully acquire a mass of merit.
examples.sa: न खलु पुनः सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन महासत्त्वेन पुण्यस्कन्धः परिग्रहीतव्यः।

examples.dm: The venerable Subhūti asked, "Blessed One, should a bodhisattva not take hold of a mass of merit?"
examples.gm: Venerable Subhūti asked, 'Blessed One, should a Bodhisattva not fully acquire a mass of merit?'
examples.sa: आयुष्मान् सुभूतिराह- ननु भगवन् बोधिसत्त्वेन पुण्यस्कन्धः परिग्रहीतव्यः ?

examples.dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, one may indeed take hold of it, but one should not take hold of it wrongly.
examples.gm: The Blessed One said, 'Subhūti, he does fully acquire it, but he does not acquire it erroneously;
examples.sa: भगवानाह-परिग्रहीतव्यः सुभूते नो ग्रहीतव्यः।

examples.dm: "They should know how to abide without dwelling on the perception of phenomena."
examples.gm: they should know them in such a way that they do not abide in the perception of a dharma.
examples.sa: तथाच ज्ञातव्या द्रष्टव्या अधिमोक्तव्याः, यथा न धर्मसंज्ञायामपि प्रत्युपतिष्ठेन्नाधर्मसंज्ञायाम्।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "perception of phenomena" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as being without perception.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, what is called 'perception of a dharma, perception of a dharma', the Tathāgata has spoken of as no perception.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? धर्मसंज्ञा धर्मसंज्ञेति सुभूते असंज्ञैषा तथागतेन भाषिता।

examples.dm: Therefore, it is called the perception of phenomena, the perception of phenomena.
examples.gm: Therefore it is called 'perception of a dharma, perception of a dharma'.
examples.sa: तेनोच्यते धर्मसंज्ञेति॥३१॥

examples.dm: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One put on his lower robe and Dharma robes, took up his alms bowl, and entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
examples.gm: Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, put on his lower garment and dharma-robe, took his alms bowl, and went to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
examples.sa: अथ खलु भगवान् पूर्वाह्णकालसमये निवास्य पात्रचीवरमादाय श्रावस्तीं महानगरीं पिण्डाय प्राविक्षत्।

examples.dm: Having finished his meal and ceased receiving alms, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robes, washed his feet, arranged his seat, sat down cross-legged, straightened his body, and remained with mindfulness established before him.
examples.gm: Having forsaken later alms-food, he put away his alms bowl and dharma-robe, washed his feet, and sat down on the prepared seat, crossing his legs, keeping his body upright, and establishing mindfulness to the fore.
examples.sa: पश्चाद्भक्तपिण्डपातप्रतिक्रान्तः पात्रचीवरं प्रतिशाम्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य न्यषीदत्प्रज्ञप्त एवासने पर्यङ्कमाभुज्य ऋजुं कायं प्रणिधाय प्रतिमुखीं स्मृतिमुपस्थाप्य।

examples.dm: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One put on his lower robe and Dharma robes, took up his alms bowl, and entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
examples.gm: Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, put on his lower garment and dharma-robe, took his alms bowl, and went to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
examples.sa: अथ खलु भगवान् पूर्वाह्णकालसमये निवास्य पात्रचीवरमादाय श्रावस्तीं महानगरीं पिण्डाय प्राविक्षत्।

examples.dm: Having finished his meal and ceased receiving alms, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robes, washed his feet, arranged his seat, sat down cross-legged, straightened his body, and remained with mindfulness established before him.
examples.gm: Having forsaken later alms-food, he put away his alms bowl and dharma-robe, washed his feet, and sat down on the prepared seat, crossing his legs, keeping his body upright, and establishing mindfulness to the fore.
examples.sa: पश्चाद्भक्तपिण्डपातप्रतिक्रान्तः पात्रचीवरं प्रतिशाम्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य न्यषीदत्प्रज्ञप्त एवासने पर्यङ्कमाभुज्य ऋजुं कायं प्रणिधाय प्रतिमुखीं स्मृतिमुपस्थाप्य।

examples.dm: How should one properly hold the mind?
examples.gm: How should they thoroughly control their mind?
examples.sa: कथं चित्तं प्रग्रहीतव्यम् ?

examples.dm: I shall explain to you how those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should dwell, how they should practice, and how they should properly hold their minds.
examples.gm: I will explain to you how one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should abide, how they should practice, and how they should thoroughly control their mind.
examples.sa: भाषिष्येऽहं ते-यथा बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन स्थातव्यं यथा प्रतिपत्तव्यं यथा चित्तं प्रग्रहीतव्यम्।

examples.bo: རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞུགས་པས། འདི་སྙམ་དུ་བདག་གིས་སེམས་ཅན་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་བསྡུ་བས་བསྡུས་པ། སྒོ་ང་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། མངལ་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། དྲོད་གཤེར་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། རྫུས་ཏེ་སྐྱེས་པའམ། གཟུགས་ཅན་ནམ། གཟུགས་ཅན་མ་ཡིན་པའམ། འདུ་ཤེས་ཅན་ནམ། འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་མིན་ནམ། སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་གདགས་པའི་བརྟགས་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཕུང་པོ་ལྷག་མ་མེད་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་དབྱིངས་སུ་ཡོངས་སུ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདའོ། །
examples.dm: Subhūti, those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: "As many sentient beings as are included in the category of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warmth and moisture, or born miraculously; whether having form or without form; whether having perception or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—all those sentient beings I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa that leaves no remainder of the aggregates."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should form this thought: 'As many beings as are subsumed in the collection of beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from heat and moisture, or miraculously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, having no perception, or neither having nor lacking perception; however many are conceptually designated as the realm of beings—all these I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates.'
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेनैव चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-यावन्तः सुभूते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वधातौ सत्त्वसंग्रहेण संगृहीता अण्डजा वा जरायुजा वा संस्वेदजा वा औपपादुका वा रूपिणो वा अरूपिणो वा संज्ञिनो वा असंज्ञिनो वा नैवसंज्ञिनो नासंज्ञिनो वा, यावान् कश्चित्सत्त्वधातुः प्रज्ञप्यमानः प्रज्ञप्यते, ते च मया सर्वेऽनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: "I shall lead all sentient beings to final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I will lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन एवं चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-सर्वे सत्त्वा मया अनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: Subhūti, in this way a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in the perception of characteristics.
examples.gm: Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts in such a way that they do not abide even in the notion of a sign.
examples.sa: एवं हि सूभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन महासत्त्वेन दानं दातव्यं यथा न निमित्तसंज्ञायामपि प्रतितिष्ठेत्।

examples.dm: Thus, one should view the Tathāgata as being without marks and signs.
examples.gm: therefore, the Tathāgata should be seen as marks and no-marks.
examples.sa: हि लक्षणालक्षणतस्तथागतो द्रष्टव्यः॥५॥

examples.dm: Subhūti, what do you think? Is it easy to measure the extent of space in the eastern direction?
examples.gm: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think it is easy to measure the space in the eastern direction?
examples.sa: तत्किं मन्यसे सुभूते सुकरं पूर्वस्यां दिशि आकाशस्य प्रमाणमुद्ग्रहीतुम् ?

examples.bo: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ། རབ་འབྱོར་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ལྷོ་དང༌། ནུབ་དང༌། བྱང་དང༌། སྟེང་དང༌། འོག་གི་ཕྱོགས་དང༌། ཕྱོགས་མཚམས་དང༌། ཕྱོགས་བཅུའི་ནམ་མཁའི་ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླའམ།
examples.dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, is it easy to measure the extent of space in the south, the west, the north, the zenith, the nadir, the intermediate directions, and the ten directions?"
examples.gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, is it easy to measure the space in the south, west, north, the directions above and below, the intermediate directions, and the ten directions?
examples.sa: भगवानाह- एवं दक्षिणपश्चिमोत्तरासु अध ऊर्ध्वं दिग्विदिक्षु समन्ताद्दशसु दिक्षु सुकरमाकाशस्य प्रमाणमुद्ग्रहीतुम् ?

examples.dm: They have not planted roots of virtue under only one Buddha.
examples.gm: nor will they have planted roots of virtue under a single Buddha.
examples.sa: नैकबुद्धावरोपितकुशलमूला भविष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: Subhūti, there will arise those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who have rendered service to many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and who have planted roots of virtue under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
examples.gm: Subhūti, there will appear those bodhisattva great beings who have served many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and planted roots of virtue under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते अनेकबुद्धशतसहस्रपर्युपासिता अनेकबुद्धशतसहस्रावरोपितकुशलमूलास्ते बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वा भविष्यन्ति,

examples.dm: They also do not engage in the perception of non-perception.
examples.gm: and they will also not engage in non-perception.
examples.sa: नापि तेषां सुभूते संज्ञा नासंज्ञा प्रवर्तते।

examples.dm: Whatever is perceived as a sentient being is itself devoid of perception.
examples.gm: Whatever is the perception of a sentient being is itself a non-perception.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? या चैषा सुभूते सत्त्वसंज्ञा, सैव असंज्ञा।

examples.dm: If one were to engage in the perception that phenomena are devoid of a self, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
examples.gm: Even if they engage in the perception of a selfless dharma, they would by that very fact grasp at a self,
examples.sa: सचेदधर्मसंज्ञा प्रवर्तेत, स एव तेषामात्मग्राहो भवेत्,

examples.dm: Subhūti, any bodhisattva who is convinced that "phenomena are selfless, phenomena are selfless," is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha.
examples.gm: Subhūti, as for any bodhisattva who resolutely believes thus: 'dharmas are without self, dharmas are without self,' the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha calls him a 'bodhisattva, a great being'.
examples.sa: यः सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वो निरात्मानो धर्मा निरात्मानो धर्मा इत्यधिमुच्यते, तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन बोधिसत्त्वो महासत्त्व इत्याख्यातः॥१७॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not grasp at phenomena as being erroneous, nor should they grasp at what is not a phenomenon.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because a bodhisattva should not wrongly grasp at a dharma, nor should they grasp at a non-dharma.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? न खलु पुनः सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन महासत्त्वेन धर्म उद्ग्रहीतव्यो नाधर्मः।

examples.dm: Therefore, keeping this in mind, the Tathāgata has said that those who understand this discourse on the Dharma as being like a raft should abandon even phenomena, let alone what are not phenomena.
examples.gm: Therefore, with this in mind, the Tathāgata has spoken: 'Those who know this dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even dharmas, let alone non-dharmas.'
examples.sa: तस्मादियं तथागतेन संधाय वाग्भाषिता-कोलोपमं धर्मपर्यायमाजानद्भिधर्मा एव प्रहातव्याः प्रागेवाधर्मा इति॥६॥

examples.dm: If some son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm world system with the seven kinds of precious substances and give them as a gift, would that son or daughter of noble family generate much merit on that basis?
examples.gm: If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?
examples.sa: यः कश्चित्कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा इमं त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रं लोकधातुं सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, अपि नु स कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा ततोनिदानं बहु पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयात्।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm of great thousand-fold world systems with the seven types of precious substances and give them as a gift, and if another were to take up from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and explain it to others and correctly demonstrate it, they would generate a mass of merit from that basis that is far greater, incalculable, and immeasurable.
examples.gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, compared to some son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, whoever takes up even just a four-line verse from this discourse on dharma, teaches it to others, and perfectly explains it will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता व इमं त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रं लोकधातुं सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भ्यः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य परेभ्यो विस्तरेण देशयेत् संप्रकाशयेत्, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयादप्रमेयसंख्येयम्।

examples.dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm of great thousand-fold world systems with the seven types of precious substances and give them as a gift, and if another were to take up from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and explain it to others and correctly demonstrate it, they would generate a mass of merit from that basis that is far greater, incalculable, and immeasurable.
examples.gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, compared to some son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, whoever takes up even just a four-line verse from this discourse on dharma, teaches it to others, and perfectly explains it will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.
examples.sa: भगवानाह-यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता व इमं त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रं लोकधातुं सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भ्यः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य परेभ्यो विस्तरेण देशयेत् संप्रकाशयेत्, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसुनुयादप्रमेयसंख्येयम्।

examples.dm: Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
examples.gm: Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
examples.sa: अथ खलु भगवांस्तस्यां वेलायामिमे गाथे अभाषत-

examples.dm: Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.
examples.gm: because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.
examples.sa: अतोनिर्जाताश्च बुद्धा भगवन्तः।

examples.bo: རབ་འབྱོར་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་དག་ངས་མཉེས་པར་བྱས་ནས་ཐུགས་འབྱུང་བར་མ་བྱས་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང༌། ཕྱི་མའི་དུས་ལྔ་བརྒྱའི་ཐ་མར་གྱུར་པ་ན། མདོ་སྡེ་འདི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། འདྲི་བ་དང༌། འཛིན་པ་དང་འཆང་བ་དང༌། ཀློག་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་ལས། རབ་འབྱོར་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སྔ་མས་བརྒྱའི་ཆར་ཡང་ཉེ་བར་མི་འགྲོ།
examples.dm: Subhūti, regarding the fact that I pleased those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and did not cause their hearts to be troubled, and regarding the fact that in the final period, in the last five hundred years, there will be those who take up, inquire into, uphold, recite, read, and fully comprehend this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that previous mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
examples.gm: Subhūti, whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, compared to whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, the former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this heap of merit;
examples.sa: यच्च मया सुभूते ते बुद्धा भगवन्त आरागिताः, आराग्य न विरागिताः, यच्च पश्चिमे काले पश्चिमे समये पश्चिमायां पञ्चशत्यां सद्धर्मविप्रलोपकाले वर्तमाने इमानेवंरूपान् सूत्रान्तानुद्ग्रहीष्यन्ति धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति, अस्य खलु पुनः सुभूते पुण्यस्कन्धस्यान्तिकादसौ पौर्वकः पुण्यस्कन्धः शततमीमपि कलां नोपैति,

examples.dm: Does a stream-enterer think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer"?
examples.gm: Does a Stream-Enterer think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer'?
examples.sa: अपि नु स्रोतआपन्नस्यैवं भवति-मया स्रोतआपत्तिफलं प्राप्तमिति?

examples.dm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a Stream-Enterer were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer', that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.sa: सचेद्भगवन् स्रोतआपन्नस्यैवं भवेत्- मया स्रोतआपत्तिफलं प्राप्तमिति, स एव तस्यात्मग्राहो भवेत्,

examples.dm: Does a once-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a once-returner'?"
examples.gm: Does a Once-Returner think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner'?
examples.sa: अपि नु सकृदागामिन एवं भवति-मया सकृदागामिफलं प्राप्तमिति ?

examples.dm: Blessed One, if a once-returner were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a once-returner," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
examples.gm: Blessed One, if a Once-Returner were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner', that itself would be his grasping at a self.

examples.dm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement.
examples.gm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? अहमस्मि भगवंस्तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन अरणाविहारिणामग्र्यो निर्दिष्टः। अहमस्मि भगवन् अर्हन् वीतरागः।

examples.dm: Blessed One, if I were to think that I had attained the state of an arhat, the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, "The son of good family, Subhūti, is the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement."
examples.gm: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained Arhatship,' the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions;
examples.sa: सचेन्मम भगवन्नेवं भवेत्-मया अर्हत्त्वं प्राप्तमिति, न मां तथागतो व्याकरिष्यदरणाविहारिणामग्र्यः सुभूतिः कुलपुत्रो

examples.dm: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, if a person were to have a body such as this, that is to say, if it were to become as large as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that body be large?
examples.gm: Subhūti, suppose, for example, a person were to have a body like this: that is, as large as Sumeru, the king of mountains. Subhūti, what do you think? Would you think that body is large?
examples.sa: तद्यथापि नाम सुभूते पुरुषो भवेदुपेतकायो महाकायो यत्तस्यैवं रूप आत्मभावः स्यात् तद्यथापि नाम सुमेरुः पर्वतराजः। तत्किं मन्यसे सुभूते अपि नु महान् स आत्मभावो भवेत् ?

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any son or daughter of noble family were to gather a heap of the seven precious substances equal in size to as many Mount Merus, the kings of mountains, as there are in the trichiliocosm, and give them as a gift, and if another person were to take from this Perfection of Wisdom even just a four-line stanza and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit would not approach even a hundredth part of the latter, nor would it bear comparison, even up to the point of calculation.
examples.gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who, having collected heaps of the seven precious substances equal in amount to however many Sumerus, kings of mountains, there are in the three thousand grand thousand world systems, gives them as a gift, if someone were to take up even just a single four-line stanza from this perfection of wisdom and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this one, up to not even bearing comparison.
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभुते स्त्री वा पुरुषो वा यावन्तस्त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रे लोकधातौ सुमेरवः पर्वतराजानः, तावतो राशीन् सप्तानां रत्नानामभिसंहृत्य तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा इतः प्रज्ञापारमिताया धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य परेभ्यो देशयेत्, अस्य सुभूते पुण्यस्कन्धस्य असौ पौर्वकः पुण्यस्कन्धः शततमीमपि कलां नोपैति, यावदुपनिषदमपि न क्षमते॥२४॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a shrine for the world including gods, humans, and asuras. It goes without saying that anyone who takes up, writes down, holds, preserves, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, what need to speak of whoever takes up this discourse on the Dharma, writes it, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and attends to it properly becoming endowed with the greatest wonder?
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते यस्मिन् पृथिवीप्रदेशे इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य भाष्येत वा संप्रकाश्येत वा, स पृथिवीप्रदेशश्चैत्यभूतो भवेत् सदेवमानुषासुरस्य लोकस्य, कः पुनर्वादो ये इमं धर्मपर्यायं सकलसमाप्तं धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति। परमेण ते सुभूते आश्चर्येण समन्वागता भविष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: That place will become like a reliquary.
examples.gm: that place will become like a stūpa.
examples.sa: चैत्यभूतः स पृथिवीप्रदेशो भविष्यति॥१५॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, that which the Tathāgata calls the perfection of patience is not a perfection.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever perfection of patience was taught by the Tathāgata, that itself is no perfection.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते या तथागतस्य क्षान्तिपारमिता, सैव अपारमिता।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven types of precious jewels and give them as a gift, and if a bodhisattva were to gain patience in the realization that phenomena are without self and unborn, then that bodhisattva would generate a mass of merit far greater, immeasurable, and incalculable than that.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven precious things and give them as a gift, and if a Bodhisattva were to attain the patience that this Dharma-discourse is selfless and unproduced, he would produce from that basis a mass of merit vastly greater, incalculable and immeasurable.
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा गङ्गानदीवालुकासमाँल्लोकधातून् सप्तरत्नपरिपूर्णं कृत्वा तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यो दानं दद्यात्, यश्च बोधिसत्त्वो निरात्मकेष्वनुत्पत्तिकेषु धर्मेषु क्षान्तिं प्रतिलभते, अयमेव ततोनिदानं बहुतरं पुण्यस्कन्धं प्रसवेदप्रमेयमसंख्येयम्।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if at that time a notion of a self had arisen in me, then a notion of malice would also have arisen.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, if at that time the perception of a self had arisen in me, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen, and
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? सचेन्मे सुभूते तस्मिन् समये आत्मसंज्ञा अभविष्यत्, व्यापादसंज्ञापि मे तस्मिन् समयेऽभविष्यत्।

examples.dm: And if a notion of a sentient being, a notion of a life-force, or a notion of a person had arisen, then a notion of malice would also have arisen.
examples.gm: because if the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life force, or the perception of a person had arisen, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen.
examples.sa: सचेत्सत्त्वसंज्ञा जीवसंज्ञा पुद्गलसंज्ञाभविष्यत्, व्यापादसंज्ञापि मे तस्मिन् समयेऽभविष्यत्।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should completely relinquish generosity for the sake of the benefit of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts in this way for the benefit of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वेन एवंरूपो दानपरित्यागः कर्तव्यः सर्वसत्त्वानामर्थाय।

examples.dm: Those sentient beings that the Tathāgata has spoken of as "all sentient beings" are also non-existent.
examples.gm: Those very sentient beings spoken of by the Tathāgata as "all sentient beings" do not exist.
examples.sa: य एवं ते सर्वसत्त्वास्तथागतेन भाषितास्त एव असत्त्वाः।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata is one who speaks what is authentic, speaks what is true, and speaks in accordance with suchness.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata speaks authentically, speaks truthfully, and speaks of suchness;
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? भूतवादी सुभूते तथागतः, सत्यवादी तथावादी अनन्यथावादी तथागतः,

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, because the term "Tathāgata" is a designation for the true suchness.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, 'Tathāgata' is a designation for true suchness.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? तथागत इति सुभूते भूततथताया एतदधिवचनम्। तथागत इति सुभूते अनुत्पादधर्मताया एतदधिवचनम्। तथागत इति सुभूते धर्मोच्छेदस्यैतदधिवचनम्। तथागत इति सुभूते अत्यन्तानुत्पन्नस्यैतदधिवचनम्। तत्कस्य हेतोः ? एष सुभूते अनुत्पादो यः परमार्थः।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any man or woman were to sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the morning, and likewise sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the midday, and again sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the evening, and in this way were to sacrifice their body for many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons;
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the morning, and were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā at midday and in the afternoon, compared to giving away bodies in this manner for many tens of millions, hundreds of millions, and hundreds of thousands of eons,
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते स्त्री वा पुरुषो वा पुर्वाह्णकालसमये गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, एवं मध्याह्नकालसमये गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, सायाह्नकालसमये गङ्गानदीवालुकासमानात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्, अनेन पर्यायेण बहूनि कल्पकोटिनियुतशतसहस्राण्यात्मभावान् परित्यजेत्,

examples.dm: Subhūti, I recall that in the past, even more incalculable than incalculable eons ago, before the time of the Tathāgata, Arhat, perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara, I served eighty-four hundred thousand million Buddhas and pleased them.
examples.gm: Subhūti, I remember that in the past, in measureless and even more than measureless eons, before and even further before the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara, eighty-four hundred thousand million myriad buddhas appeared, whom I pleased,
examples.sa: अभिजानाम्यहं सुभूते अतीतेऽध्वन्यसंख्येयैः कल्पैरसंख्येयतरैर्दीपंकरस्य तथागतस्यार्हतः सम्यक्संबुद्धस्य परेण परतरेण चतुरशीतिबुद्धकोटिनियुतशतसहस्राण्यभूवन् ये मयारागिताः,

examples.dm: One should know that the ripening of this is also inconceivable.
examples.gm: its ripening should also be known as inconceivable.

examples.dm: You should know that its ripening is also inconceivable.
examples.gm: and its ripening should also be known to be simply inconceivable.
examples.sa: अस्य अचिन्त्य एव विपाकः प्रतिकाङ्क्षितव्यः॥१६॥

examples.dm: nor can those who hold the view of a self, those who hold the view of a sentient being, those who hold the view of a life-force,
examples.gm: nor by those who hold a view of a self, nor by those who hold a view of a sentient being, nor by those who hold a view of a living being;
examples.sa: नात्मदृष्टिकैर्न सत्त्वदृष्टिकैर्न जीवदृष्टिकैर्न पुद्गलदृष्टिकैः।

examples.dm: and were to say, "The Tathāgata has spoken of a view of a sentient being, a view of a life-force, and a view of a person," would that person be speaking correctly?
examples.gm: the Tathāgata has spoken of the view of a sentient being, the view of a living soul, and the view of a person'—if they said that, would they be speaking truthfully?
examples.sa: सत्त्वदृष्टिर्जीवदृष्टिः पुद्गलदृष्टिस्तथागतेन भाषिता, अपि नु स सुभूते सम्यग्वदमानो वदेत् ?

examples.dm: nor can those who hold the view of a self, those who hold the view of a sentient being, those who hold the view of a life-force,
examples.gm: nor by those who hold a view of a self, nor by those who hold a view of a sentient being, nor by those who hold a view of a living being;
examples.sa: नात्मदृष्टिकैर्न सत्त्वदृष्टिकैर्न जीवदृष्टिकैर्न पुद्गलदृष्टिकैः।

examples.dm: and were to say, "The Tathāgata has spoken of a view of a sentient being, a view of a life-force, and a view of a person," would that person be speaking correctly?
examples.gm: the Tathāgata has spoken of the view of a sentient being, the view of a living soul, and the view of a person'—if they said that, would they be speaking truthfully?
examples.sa: सत्त्वदृष्टिर्जीवदृष्टिः पुद्गलदृष्टिस्तथागतेन भाषिता, अपि नु स सुभूते सम्यग्वदमानो वदेत् ?

examples.dm: or those who hold the view of a person listen to it, take it up, grasp it, read it, or master it.
examples.gm: and those who hold a view of a person are unable to hear, take up, hold, read, or completely comprehend it,
examples.sa: नाबोधिसत्त्वप्रतिज्ञै सत्त्वैः शक्यमयं धर्मपर्यायः श्रोतुं वा उद्ग्रहीतुं वा धारयितुं वा वाचयितुं वा पर्यवाप्तुं वा।

examples.dm: and were to say, "The Tathāgata has spoken of a view of a sentient being, a view of a life-force, and a view of a person," would that person be speaking correctly?
examples.gm: the Tathāgata has spoken of the view of a sentient being, the view of a living soul, and the view of a person'—if they said that, would they be speaking truthfully?
examples.sa: सत्त्वदृष्टिर्जीवदृष्टिः पुद्गलदृष्टिस्तथागतेन भाषिता, अपि नु स सुभूते सम्यग्वदमानो वदेत् ?

examples.dm: Subhūti, if there were any phenomenon that the Tathāgata had fully realized as enlightenment, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have given me the prophecy, saying, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
examples.gm: Subhūti, if there had been some dharma by which the Tathāgata fully awakened, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'
examples.sa: सचेत्पुनः सुभूते कश्चिद्धर्मस्तथागतेनाभिसंबुद्धोऽभविष्यत्, न मां दीपंकरस्तथागतो व्याकरिष्यत्-भविष्यसि त्वं माणव अनागतेऽध्वनि शाक्यमुनिर्नाम तथागतोऽर्हन् सम्यक्संबुद्ध इति।

examples.dm: for that reason, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
examples.gm: therefore the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'
examples.sa: तस्मादहं दीपंकरेण तथागतेन व्याकृत- भविष्यसि त्वं माणव अनागतेऽध्वनि शाक्यमुनिर्नाम तथागतोऽर्हन् सम्यक्संबुद्ध।

examples.dm: Subhūti, if there were any phenomenon that the Tathāgata had fully realized as enlightenment, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have given me the prophecy, saying, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
examples.gm: Subhūti, if there had been some dharma by which the Tathāgata fully awakened, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'

examples.dm: The guides are the Dharmakāya; since the nature of reality is not an object to be known, it cannot be cognized.

examples.dm: Subhūti, if you think that those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle hold the view that any phenomenon is destroyed or designated as cut off, Subhūti, you should not view it in that way.
examples.gm: Subhūti, if you think that those who have genuinely set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle have destroyed some phenomenon or designated it as annihilated, Subhūti, it should not be seen like that.
examples.sa: न खलु पुनस्ते सुभूते कश्चिदेवं वदेत्-बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितैः कस्यचिद्धर्मस्य विनाशः प्रज्ञप्तः उच्छेदो वेति। न खलु पुनस्ते सुभूते एवं द्रष्टव्यम्। तत्कस्य हेतोः ?

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a noble son or a noble daughter were to take all the earth-dust particles in the trichiliocosm world-system and reduce them to a collection of the finest atoms, what do you think, Subhūti? Would that collection of the finest atoms be numerous?
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any son of good family or daughter of good family were to grind as many particles of earth as there are in the trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world system, into powder so that they become, for example, like a mass of fine atoms, what do you think, Subhūti, would that mass of fine atoms be large?
examples.sa: यश्च खलु पुनः सुभूते कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा यावन्ति त्रिसाहस्रमहासाहस्रे लोकधातौ पृथिवीरजांसि, तावतां लोकधातूनामेवंरूपं मषिं कुर्यात् यावदेवमसंख्येयेन वीर्येण तद्यथापि नाम परमाणुसंचयः, तत्किं मन्यसे सुभूते-अपि नु बहुः स परमाणुसंचयो भवेत् ?

examples.dm: The Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s park, together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks and a vast number of bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

examples.gm: Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, put on his lower garment and dharma-robe, took his alms bowl, and went to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
examples.sa: अथ खलु भगवान् पूर्वाह्णकालसमये निवास्य पात्रचीवरमादाय श्रावस्तीं महानगरीं पिण्डाय प्राविक्षत्।

examples.dm: Having finished his meal and ceased receiving alms, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robes, washed his feet, arranged his seat, sat down cross-legged, straightened his body, and remained with mindfulness established before him.
examples.gm: Having forsaken later alms-food, he put away his alms bowl and dharma-robe, washed his feet, and sat down on the prepared seat, crossing his legs, keeping his body upright, and establishing mindfulness to the fore.

examples.dm: Subhūti, those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: "As many sentient beings as are included in the category of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warmth and moisture, or born miraculously; whether having form or without form; whether having perception or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—all those sentient beings I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa that leaves no remainder of the aggregates."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should form this thought: 'As many beings as are subsumed in the collection of beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from heat and moisture, or miraculously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, having no perception, or neither having nor lacking perception; however many are conceptually designated as the realm of beings—all these I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates.'

examples.dm: "Even though immeasurable sentient beings are thus led to complete nirvāṇa, one should generate the mind thinking that not even one sentient being has been led to complete nirvāṇa."
examples.gm: One should generate the mind thinking: 'Even though immeasurable beings have thus been led to complete nirvāṇa, no being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.'
examples.sa: एवमपरिमाणानपि सत्त्वान् परिनिर्वाप्य न कश्चित्सत्त्वः परिनिर्वापितो भवति।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person, they should not be called a bodhisattva.
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because if one holds the notion of a being, holds the notion of a living soul, or holds the notion of a person, they would not be called a bodhisattva.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? न स सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वो वक्तव्यो यस्य सत्त्वसंज्ञा प्रवर्तेत, जीवसंज्ञा वा पुद्गलसंज्ञा व प्रवर्तेत॥३॥

examples.dm: Subhūti, in the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, there will arise Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who are endowed with morality, endowed with qualities, and endowed with wisdom.
examples.gm: Subhūti, in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, there will appear bodhisattva great beings who possess ethical discipline, possess good qualities, and possess wisdom.
examples.sa: सुभूते भविष्यन्त्यनागतेऽध्वनि बोधिसत्त्वा महासत्त्वाः पश्चिमे काले पश्चिमे समये पश्चिमायां पञ्चशत्यां सद्धर्मविप्रलोपे वर्तमाने गुणवन्तः शीलवन्तः प्रज्ञावन्तश्च भविष्यन्ति, ये इमेष्वेवंरूपेषु सूत्रान्तपदेषु भाष्यमाणेषु भूतसंज्ञामुत्पादयिष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a shrine for the world including gods, humans, and asuras. It goes without saying that anyone who takes up, writes down, holds, preserves, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, what need to speak of whoever takes up this discourse on the Dharma, writes it, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and attends to it properly becoming endowed with the greatest wonder?
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभुते यस्मिन् पृथिवीप्रदेशे इतो धर्मपर्यायादन्तशश्चतुष्पादिकामपि गाथामुद्गृह्य भाष्येत वा संप्रकाश्येत वा, स पृथिवीप्रदेशश्चैत्यभूतो भवेत् सदेवमानुषासुरस्य लोकस्य, कः पुनर्वादो ये इमं धर्मपर्यायं सकलसमाप्तं धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति। परमेण ते सुभूते आश्चर्येण समन्वागता भविष्यन्ति।

examples.dm: Blessed One, ever since I attained the eye of wisdom, I have never before heard such a discourse on Dharma as this.

examples.gm: Why is that? Because, Bhagavān, whatever is a true perception is itself no perception.

examples.gm: Bhagavān, in the future time, in the final five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write, hold, keep, read, and completely master this discourse on Dharma will be endowed with supreme wonder.

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, that which the Tathāgata calls the perfection of patience is not a perfection.

examples.gm: Subhūti, I remember that in the past, for five hundred lifetimes, when I was the sage called Kṣāntivādin, even at that time the perception of a self did not arise in me.

examples.gm: Why is that? Because whatever is an abiding is itself a non-abiding.
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? यत्प्रतिष्ठितं तदेवाप्रतिष्ठितम्।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, there is neither truth nor falsehood in the phenomena that the Tathāgata has perfectly awakened to or taught.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, in whatever phenomena the Tathāgata has fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते यस्तथागतेन धर्मोऽभिसंबुद्धो देशितो निध्यातः, न तत्र सत्यं न मृषा।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, it is like this: for example, when dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with sight sees all various kinds of forms; in the same way, one should view a bodhisattva who practices generosity without having fallen into the perception of entities.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, it is like this: just as when dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with eyes sees various forms, in the same way should a bodhisattva be seen who has not fallen into objects when giving gifts.
examples.sa: तद्यथापि नाम सुभूते चक्षुष्मान् पुरुषः प्रभातायां रात्रौ सूर्येऽभ्युद्गते नानविधानि रूपाणि पश्येत्, एवमवस्तुपतितो बोधिसत्त्वो द्रष्टव्यो योऽवस्तुपतितो दानं परित्यजति॥

examples.dm: The Tathāgata has spoken this Dharma discourse for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the unsurpassed vehicle.
examples.gm: The Tathāgata has spoken this dharma discourse for the sake of sentient beings who have authentically entered into the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of sentient beings who have authentically entered into the foremost vehicle.
examples.sa: अयं च सुभूते धर्मपर्यायस्तथागतेन भाषितोऽग्रयानसंप्रस्थितानां सत्त्वानामर्थाय, श्रेष्ठयानसंप्रस्थितानां सत्त्वानामर्थाय।

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, those who are intent upon the inferior cannot listen to this discourse on the Dharma,
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, those who are inclined toward the inferior are unable to hear this dharma discourse;
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? न हि शक्यं सुभूते अयं धर्मपर्यायो हीनाधिमुक्तिकैः सत्त्वैः श्रोतुम्,

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where this sūtra is taught will be worthy of being venerated by the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, in whatever place this sūtra is taught, that place will become worthy of being venerated by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.
examples.sa: अपि तु खलु पुनः सुभूते यत्र पृथिवीप्रदेशे इदं सूत्रं प्रकशयिष्यते, पूजनीयः स पृथिवीप्रदेशो भविष्यति सदेवमानुषासुरस्य लोकस्य।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up, uphold, bear, read, and master these words of such a sūtra will be tormented,
examples.gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whichever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up, hold, keep, read, and completely comprehend these words of a sūtra such as this, they will be tormented;
examples.sa: अपि तु ये ते सुभूते कुलपुत्रा वा कुलदुहितरो वा इमानेवंरूपान् सूत्रान्तानुद्ग्रहीष्यन्ति धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, योनिशश्च मनसिकरिष्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति, ते परिभूता भविष्यन्ति,

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, those sentient beings who, in previous lives, committed non-virtuous actions that would have led to rebirth in the lower realms, will, by being tormented in this very life, have those non-virtuous actions of previous lives that would have led to rebirth in the lower realms purified;
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, because they are tormented in this very life for whatever nonvirtuous actions those sentient beings committed in past lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms, the nonvirtuous actions they committed in past lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms will be purified,
examples.sa: तत्कस्य हेतोः ? यानि च तेषां सुभूते सत्त्वानां पौर्वजन्मिकान्यशुभानि कर्माणि कृतान्यपायसंवर्तनीयानि, दृष्ट एव धर्मे परिभूततया तानि पौर्वजन्मिकान्यशुभानि कर्माणि क्षपयिष्यन्ति,

examples.dm: Subhūti, regarding the fact that I pleased those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and did not cause their hearts to be troubled, and regarding the fact that in the final period, in the last five hundred years, there will be those who take up, inquire into, uphold, recite, read, and fully comprehend this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that previous mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
examples.gm: Subhūti, whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, compared to whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, the former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this heap of merit;
examples.sa: यच्च मया सुभूते ते बुद्धा भगवन्त आरागिताः, आराग्य न विरागिताः, यच्च पश्चिमे काले पश्चिमे समये पश्चिमायां पञ्चशत्यां सद्धर्मविप्रलोपकाले वर्तमाने इमानेवंरूपान् सूत्रान्तानुद्ग्रहीष्यन्ति धारयिष्यन्ति वाचयिष्यन्ति पर्यवाप्स्यन्ति, परेभ्यश्च विस्तरेण संप्रकाशयिष्यन्ति, अस्य खलु पुनः सुभूते पुण्यस्कन्धस्यान्तिकादसौ पौर्वकः पुण्यस्कन्धः शततमीमपि कलां नोपैति,

examples.dm: Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: "I shall lead all sentient beings to final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder."
examples.gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I will lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.
examples.sa: इह सुभूते बोधिसत्त्वयानसंप्रस्थितेन एवं चित्तमुत्पादयितव्यम्-सर्वे सत्त्वा मया अनुपधिशेषे निर्वाणधातौ परिनिर्वापयितव्याः।

examples.dm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings are led to final nirvāṇa in this way, one should generate the mind with the thought that not even one sentient being has been led to final nirvāṇa.
examples.gm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings have been led to complete nirvāṇa in this way, no sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa'—thus should they generate the mind.
examples.sa: एवं स सत्त्वान् परिनिर्वाप्य न कश्चित्सत्त्वः परिनिर्वापितो भवति।

examples.dm: for that reason, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
examples.gm: therefore the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'

examples.dm: Why is that? Subhūti, that which is called "teaching the Dharma" is such that there is no phenomenon whatsoever that can be apprehended as "teaching the Dharma" or "the Dharma that is taught."
examples.gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'teaching the Dharma', there is no Dharma whatsoever that can be apprehended as 'teaching the Dharma'.

examples.dm: Blessed One, in future times, will there be sentient beings who, upon hearing such an explanation of the Dharma as this, will give rise to true faith?
examples.gm: "Blessed One, in the future, will there be any sentient beings who, having heard such a teaching of the Dharma, will come to truly believe it?"
examples.sa: अस्ति भगवन् केचित्सत्त्वा भविष्यन्त्यनागतेऽध्वनि पश्चिमे काले पश्चिमे समये पश्चिमायां पञ्चशत्यां सद्धर्मविप्रलोपे वर्तमाने, य इमानेवंरूपान् धर्मान् श्रुत्वा अभिश्रद्धास्यन्ति।

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any son or daughter of noble family were to gather a heap of the seven precious substances equal in size to as many Mount Merus, the kings of mountains, as there are in the trichiliocosm, and give them as a gift, and if another person were to take from this Perfection of Wisdom even just a four-line stanza and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit would not approach even a hundredth part of the latter, nor would it bear comparison, even up to the point of calculation.
examples.gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who, having collected heaps of the seven precious substances equal in amount to however many Sumerus, kings of mountains, there are in the three thousand grand thousand world systems, gives them as a gift, if someone were to take up even just a single four-line stanza from this perfection of wisdom and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this one, up to not even bearing comparison.

examples.dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven types of precious jewels and give them as a gift, and if a bodhisattva were to gain patience in the realization that phenomena are without self and unborn, then that bodhisattva would generate a mass of merit far greater, immeasurable, and incalculable than that.

examples.dm: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond" is concluded.
examples.gm: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra called the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā is complete.
examples.sa: आर्यवज्रच्छेदिका भगवती प्रज्ञापारमिता समाप्ता॥

examples.dm: Namo bhagavate prajñāpāramitāye. Oṃ natadatita iliśi iliśi miliśi miliśi bhinayan bhinayan. Namo bhagavate pratyampate iriti iriti miriti miriti śuriti śuriti uśuri uśuri bhuyuye bhuyuye svāhā.
examples.gm: namo bhagavate prajñāpāramitāye oṃ natadatita iliśi iliśi miliśi miliśi bhinayan bhinayan namo bhagavate pratyaṃprate iriti iriti mirati miriti śuriti śuriti uśuri uśuri bhuyuye bhuyuye svāhā

examples.dm: Reciting this essence of the Diamond Cutter once is equivalent to reading the Diamond Cutter nineteen thousand times.
examples.gm: By reciting this essence of the Vajracchedikā once, it becomes equal to having read the Vajracchedikā ninety million times.
